messages.subject: Bar Chart Help
parts:
Hi,

The problem I am facing is "outlier values" distorting the axis. Specifically. "Delta" values of 4215 and -15.

Here is how it goes:

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(scales)

# read input file
df.1 = read.csv(file = "Mind the Gap v3.csv",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

df.2 <- df.1 %>%
  select(Season,Division, Level,X)

df.2$Delta = as.numeric(gsub("%","",df.2$X))

df.3 <- df.2 %>%
  filter(Level != "Avg") %>%
  arrange(Delta)

df.4 = df.3 %>%
  select(Season,Level,Delta)

p3 = ggplot(df.4, aes (x = Level,y = Delta, fill = Season)) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = position_dodge(),
    size = .3
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1000, 4500)) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),    # Remove y - axis label
    legend.position = c(.90, .85)   # legend inside plot
  )


#p4 = p3 + scale_y_continuous(trans = log2_trans()) # to allow the smaller y value to appear

p4 = p3 + ggtitle ("Variation in Average Wage \n Over the Years")

p4


Here is the data 

> dput(df.1)
structure(list(Season = c("1984-85", "1984-85", "1984-85", "1984-85", 
"1984-85", "2014-15", "2014-15", "2014-15", "2014-15", "2014-15"
), Division = c("Division One", "Division Two", "Division Three", 
"Division Four", "Average", "Premier League", "Championship", 
"League One", "League Two", "Average"), Level = c("1", "2", "3", 
"4", "Avg", "1", "2", "3", "4", "Avg"), Average.Wage = c("24,900", 
"15,500", "11,200", "8,300", "9,800", "1,700,000", "324,200", 
"69,500", "40,300", "39,400"), Difference.From.Average = c("15100", 
"5700", "1400", "-1500", " -   ", "1660600", "284800", "30100", 
"900", " -   "), X = c("154%", "58%", "14%", "-15%", "", "4215%", 
"723%", "76%", "2%", "")), .Names = c("Season", "Division", "Level", 
"Average.Wage", "Difference.From.Average", "X"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-10L))


And lastly any suggestions on how to spice up the graph to make it look like an "infographic"


Br /

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: Bar Chart Help
parts:
>The problem I am facing is "outlier values" distorting the axis.
>Specifically. "Delta" values of 4215 and -15.

My only real suggestion is to not express them as deviations from the
mean. That handles the lower end (if you want the means in there, maybe
put them in as horizontal lines?). You're stuck with the top end being
skewed. Surely that is the whole point of the Premier League's existence.

Looking at the data I did wonder why the overall average for the 2014-15
season was less than all of the values for the divisions.

>>And lastly any suggestions on how to spice up the graph to make it look
>>like an "infographic"

Well you might mess about with plotting them as points with the size
determined by the wage. (maybe x as level, y as season; or the same y for
both seasons with different colours for seasons, a bit of jitter (?) and
alpha < 1).

Ron.

messages.author: 26c1dcb4f0b4b25b
messages.subject: Re: Bar Chart Help
parts:
Hi,

You can do logarithmic scaling to reduce the skewness in the values.
But that would definitely mean that you will have to mention that the DELTA is actually LOG(DELTA)

Regards,
Anant
